newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BONDS HOMERS TO LEAD GIANTS PAST ASTROS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BONDS HOMERS TO LEAD GIANTS PAST ASTROS.

text.p: Barry Bonds led off the bottom of the ninth inning with his first home run in 10 days, giving the San Francisco Giants a 4-3 victory over the Houston Astros Monday.
Bonds drilled a 1-0 pitch from Jose Lima (0-3) into the right-field bleachers for his eighth homer of the season.
"It feels so good just to win because we haven't been playing very well," he said. "And it feels good for me to finally help the club a little bit instead of what I have been doing lately."

Bonds had three hits for the Giants, who won in their last at-bat for the eighth time this season. The surprise National League West leaders have come from behind in half of their 28 wins and improved to 10-5 in one-run games.
"Each day, someome else is going to be the hero and that's a great quality for a team to have," said Giants infielder Bill Mueller.
Bonds' blast gave Julian Tavarez (1-2) his first National League win. The former Cleveland Indian got the last out in the top of the ninth after allowing a single to Craig Biggio.
Biggio had four hits and scored twice for the Astros, who have lost eight of their last 12 on the road.
In Pittsburgh, Kevin Foster and two relievers combined on a three-hitter and the Chicago Cubs edged the Pirates 2-1 in a game that saw two inside-the-park homers in the same inning.

Chicago's Sammy Sosa had an inside-the-park homer in the top of the sixth and Pittsburgh's Tony Womack did it in the bottom. It is believed to be the first time in major-league history that different teams hit inside-the-park homers in the same inning.

The last time there were two inside-the-park homers in the same game was October 4, 1986, when Minnesota's Greg Gagne had two himself. The last National League game with two inside-the-park homers was June 18, 1976, when Lou Brock and Hector Cruz did it for St Louis.
It was the 13th homer of the season for Sosa, who has four homers in his last five games, nine in his last 14 games and is batting .395 (32-for-81) in his last 20 contests.

Centre fielder Adrian Brown and right fielder Jose Guillen -- both rookies -- converged on Sosa's fly ball and the ball bounced off Brown's glove toward right field. The relay from Brown to Womack to catcher Jason Kendall appeared to get there in time but Sosa slid headfirst and was called safe.

In the bottom half, Womack hit a line drive to centre that Doug Glanville dove for and missed. The ball rolled all the way to the wall, where Sosa, the right fielder, retrieved it. But the relay was late and Womack slid in well before the tag.

In San Diego, Michael Tucker had three hits and drove in three runs and five relievers combined to allow one run and five hits over the final 6 2/3 innnings as the Atlanta Braves routed the Padres 12-5.
Jeff Blauser added three hits and a pair of RBI and Kenny Lofton had two hits and two RBI.
Every Atlanta starting position player had a hit and all but Ryan Klesko scored a run. The Braves used a 16-hit attack to post their sixth straight win over San Diego.
In Cincinnati, the Reds swept a doubleheader with the Philadelphia Phillies.
In the opener, Bret Boone capped a five-run third inning with a two-run homer as the Reds won 8-5 and John Smiley (5-6) won for the fourth time in five starts.
Gregg Jefferies hit a two-run homer and Kevin Jordan added a solo shot for Philadelphia, which has lost four of five.
In the nightcap, Mike Morgan (2-4) allowed three runs and six hits in seven innings and Barry Larkin went 3-for-3 with a walk as the Reds won 8-4.

Larkin, who left in the seventh after the Reds built an 8-3 lead, has reached base safely in 12 straight plate appearances. He is within two of Pedro Guerrero's National League record of reaching in 14 straight appearances.

At Colorado, Andres Galarraga hit a two-run homer and Vinny Castilla followed with a home run off reliever Mark Petkovsek (2-4) in the eighth as the Rockies rallied from a 6-0 deficit and defeated the St Louis Cardinals 9-7.

Galarraga drove in four runs and Walt Weiss added a two-run homer for the Rockies. Galarraga's 469-foot blast was the second longest by a Rockie at Coors Field, surpassed only by a 475-foot homer by Larry Walker.
Ron Gant hit a three-run homer and Gary Gaetti had three hits, including a solo home run, for the Cardinals.
In Los Angeles, Eric Karros hit a two-run homer and Chan Ho Park (3-2) pitched 6 2/3 strong innings as the Dodgers beat the Florida Marlins 5-3 for their third straight win.
Raul Mondesi and Todd Zeile added solo homers for the Dodgers. Kurt Abbott and Cliff Floyd homered for Florida.

In Montreal, Rey Ordonez's two-out RBI single in the top of the eighth capped a three-run rally and Greg McMichael pitched out of a bases-loaded, none-out jam in the bottom of the frame as the New York Mets beat the Expos 4-3.
Rookie Cory Lidle (3-0) notched the win despite allowing a run and two hits in one inning. John Franco tossed a perfect ninth for his 14th save in 16 opportunities.
The win was the Mets'19th in their last 27 games and moved them five games over .500 for the first time this season.
